title: Master and Man
text:
Vasili Brekhunov was a prosperous village merchant who measured everything in money. One winter evening he set out by sledge with his servant Nikita, a gentle, hardworking peasant he routinely underpaid, to close a deal on a forest before rival buyers could. A snowstorm was rising, but he would not wait.

They lost the road again and again and at last had to stop in an open field. Nikita settled into the sledge, resigned to whatever came. In the night Vasili, unable to sleep and terrified, mounted the horse and rode off alone, leaving Nikita to freeze. In the dark and the blowing snow he rode in a circle and ended up back at the sledge.

There he found Nikita nearly frozen. Something changed in Vasili. He opened his fur coat, lay down on top of his servant, and covered him with his own body and warmth. Lying there through the night, he felt a joy he had never known, and he thought that Nikita was alive, and so he himself was alive.

By morning, Vasili was dead. Nikita was found alive under him. He lost some toes to frostbite, but he lived for twenty more years.
lesson: Power over others is easy to treat as a source of profit. Its real meaning shows when the people who depend on you are in danger and you choose to shield them.
